claim: TMEM16A is a ligand-gated anion channel that is activated by intracellular Ca2+
source: TMEM16A is a ligand-gated anion channel that is activated by intracellular Ca2+.
evidence: This is a fundamental characterization of TMEM16A stated in the abstract, supported by the experimental work presented in the manuscript.

claim: TMEM16A comprises two independent pores
source: This channel comprises two independent pores and closely apposed Ca2+ binding sites that are contained within each subunit of a homodimeric protein.
evidence: Stated in the abstract and supported by structural and functional data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Ca2+ binding sites are contained within each subunit of a homodimeric protein
source: This channel comprises two independent pores and closely apposed Ca2+ binding sites that are contained within each subunit of a homodimeric protein.
evidence: Stated in the abstract and supported by structural data.

claim: Positively charged pore-lining residues influence anion conduction in TMEM16A
source: Previously we characterized the influence of positively charged pore-lining residues on anion conduction (Paulino et al., 2017a).
evidence: Referenced from prior work by the authors.

claim: Currents of constitutively active mutants lose their outward rectification as a function of Ca2+ concentration
source: The currents of constitutively active mutants lose their outward rectification as a function of Ca2+ concentration due to the alleviation of energy barriers for anion conduction.
evidence: Stated in the abstract and demonstrated by experimental data in Figure 1C.

claim: The loss of outward rectification originates from Coulombic interactions between bound Ca2+ and permeating anions
source: This phenomenon originates from Coulombic interactions between the bound Ca2+ and permeating anions and thus demonstrates that an electrostatic gate imposed by the vacant binding site present in the sterically open pore, is released by Ca2+ binding to enable an otherwise sub-conductive pore to conduct with full capacity.
evidence: Stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data and Poisson-Boltzmann calculations.

claim: An electrostatic gate imposed by the vacant binding site is released by Ca2+ binding
source: This phenomenon originates from Coulombic interactions between the bound Ca2+ and permeating anions and thus demonstrates that an electrostatic gate imposed by the vacant binding site present in the sterically open pore, is released by Ca2+ binding to enable an otherwise sub-conductive pore to conduct with full capacity.
evidence: Stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript.

claim: The TMEM16 family encompasses ion channels and lipid scramblases with a common conserved molecular architecture
source: The calcium-activated chloride channel TMEM16A is part of a large family of membrane proteins that encompasses ion channels and lipid scramblases with a common conserved molecular architecture (Brunner et al., 2016; Caputo et al., 2008; Picollo et al., 2015; Schroeder et al., 2008; Terashima et al., 2013; Whitlock and Hartzell, 2017; Yang et al., 2008).
evidence: Stated in the introduction with multiple supporting citations.

claim: The TMEM16 family is related to mechanosensitive channels of the OSCA and TMC families
source: With respect to their fold, the TMEM16 family is related to mechanosensitive channels of the OSCA and TMC families (Ballesteros et al., 2018; Pan et al., 2018; Zhang et al., 2018).
evidence: Stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: TMEM16A is widely expressed and contributes to important physiological processes
source: TMEM16A is widely expressed and contributes to important physiological processes including the transport of chloride across epithelia and the control of electrical signal transduction in smooth muscle and certain neurons (Huang et al., 2012; Oh and Jung, 2016; Scudieri et al., 2012).
evidence: Stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: TMEM16A harbors two ion conduction pores, each contained within a single subunit of a homodimeric protein
source: TMEM16A harbors two ion conduction pores, each contained within a single subunit of a homodimeric protein (Figure 1A).
evidence: Stated in the introduction and shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Both pores in TMEM16A function independently
source: Both pores function independently and are activated by the binding of two Ca2+ ions to a site embedded within the membrane-inserted part of each subunit close to the ion conduction path (Jeng et al., 2016; Lim et al., 2016).
evidence: Stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: TMEM16A pores are activated by the binding of two Ca2+ ions
source: Both pores function independently and are activated by the binding of two Ca2+ ions to a site embedded within the membrane-inserted part of each subunit close to the ion conduction path (Jeng et al., 2016; Lim et al., 2016).
evidence: Stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: In the open conformation, anions access the narrow neck of an hourglass-shaped pore via water-filled vestibules
source: In the open conformation, anions access the narrow neck of an hourglass-shaped pore via water-filled vestibules from the extra- and intracellular sides and permeate through the constricted part presumably after shedding most of their coordinating water molecules (Betto et al., 2014; Dang et al., 2017; Ni et al., 2014; Paulino et al., 2017a; Qu and Hartzell, 2000).
evidence: Stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: The energetic penalty for dehydration is surmounted by positive charges placed on both sides of the neck
source: During this process, the energetic penalty for dehydration is surmounted by positive charges placed on both sides of the neck (Paulino et al., 2017b).
evidence: Stated in the introduction with supporting citation.

claim: In the apo conformation, the Ca2+ binding site is accessible from the cytoplasm
source: In the apo conformation, the Ca2+ binding site is accessible from the cytoplasm (Paulino et al., 2017a).
evidence: Stated in the introduction with supporting citation.

claim: The binding of Ca2+ favors conformational changes in the pore-lining helix α6
source: The binding of Ca2+ favors conformational changes in the pore-lining helix α6, which provides polar and acidic sidechains that coordinate the bound cations and thus directly couples ligand binding to pore opening (Paulino et al., 2017a; Peters et al., 2018).
evidence: Stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Helix α6 provides polar and acidic sidechains that coordinate the bound cations
source: The binding of Ca2+ favors conformational changes in the pore-lining helix α6, which provides polar and acidic sidechains that coordinate the bound cations and thus directly couples ligand binding to pore opening (Paulino et al., 2017a; Peters et al., 2018).
evidence: Stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: The closure of the aqueous access pathway to the ligand binding site buries the bound calcium ions within the transmembrane electric field
source: The subsequent closure of the aqueous access pathway to the ligand binding site buries the bound calcium ions within the transmembrane electric field, which mechanistically accounts for the observed voltage dependence of activation by modulating the binding affinity of Ca2+ (Arreola et al., 1996; Brunner et al., 2014; Xiao et al., 2011).
evidence: Stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: The movement of helix α6 relays a conformational change towards the neck to release a steric barrier
source: The movement of the helix relays a conformational change towards the neck to release a steric barrier, which acts as a gate in the closed conformation of the channel (Paulino et al., 2017a).
evidence: Stated in the introduction with supporting citation.

claim: The bound Ca2+ ions change the charge distribution at the wide intracellular vestibule thereby removing an electrostatic barrier
source: Additionally, the bound Ca2+ ions change the charge distribution at the wide intracellular vestibule thereby removing a second, electrostatic barrier that specifically hinders the access of anions in the ligand-free state (Paulino et al., 2017a).
evidence: Stated in the introduction with supporting citation.

claim: Long-range Coulombic interactions underlie an electrostatic gating mechanism in TMEM16A
source: These long-range interactions underlie an electrostatic gating mechanism that acts through space and that is synergistic with the opening of a steric gate, allowing an otherwise sub-conductive pore to conduct with full capacity.
evidence: Stated in the introduction and supported by experimental data and calculations throughout the manuscript.

claim: The G644P mutation increases the potency of Ca2+ and results in constitutive activity
source: In this mutant, the replacement of a flexible glycine at a hinge in α6 (Gly 644, Figure 1B) with a rigid proline increases the potency of Ca2+ and concomitantly results in constitutive activity (Paulino et al., 2017a).
evidence: Stated in the Results section with supporting citation and experimental data.

claim: The basal current of G644P is highly outwardly rectifying
source: The basal current of this mutant is highly outwardly rectifying but it progressively loses its rectification at increasing Ca2+ concentrations until it becomes pseudo-linear in saturating conditions (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: Stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The instantaneous currents of WT are linear in the entire Ca2+ concentration range
source: This differs from the instantaneous currents of WT, which are linear in the entire Ca2+ concentration range (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: The effect of Ca2+ on G644P originates from the alleviation of local energy barriers for anion conduction at the intracellular entrance and the center of the pore
source: When analyzed with our described minimal model of ion permeation, this effect seems to originate from the alleviation of local energy barriers for anion conduction at the intracellular entrance and the center of the pore as a function of Ca2+ concentration (Figure 1D).
evidence: Stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The lowering of energy barriers can be described by a binding isotherm with EC50 values of 60 nM and 170 nM for the inner and central barriers respectively
source: The lowering of the energy barriers can be described by a binding isotherm with EC50 values of 60 nM and 170 nM, and Hill coefficients of 2.1 and 1.7 at 80 mV for the inner and the central barriers respectively (Figure 1E).
evidence: Stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 1E.

claim: The Q649A mutant displays a left-shifted EC50 and basal current that is equally outwardly rectifying as G644P
source: Like G644P, this mutant displays a left-shifted EC50 and basal current that is equally outwardly rectifying (Figure 1—figure supplement 3A).
evidence: Stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3A.

claim: The potency of Ca2+ is increased upon depolarization in Q649A
source: At the membrane potentials tested, we observed a similar effect of Ca2+ on the energetics of anion conduction as in G644P (Figure 1C–F) and as with steady-state concentration-responses, the potency of Ca2+ is increased upon depolarization (Figure 1F–G, Figure 1—figure supplement 3B–D).
evidence: Stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 1F-G and Figure 1—figure supplement 3B-D.

claim: Mg2+ acts as a low affinity competitive antagonist that lowers the potency of Ca2+
source: Although Mg2+ is incapable of activating WT even at high concentrations (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A), it acts as a low affinity competitive antagonist that lowers the potency of Ca2+, indicating that it might occupy the Ca2+ binding site (Ni et al., 2014).
evidence: Stated in the Results section with supporting citation and experimental data.

claim: Mg2+ produces a concentration-dependent reduction of the outward rectification in G644P
source: This is confirmed in the mutant G644P, for which we observed a concentration-dependent reduction of the outward rectification in the presence of Mg2+ (Figure 2A).
evidence: Stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Mg2+ appears to 'activate' G644P by primarily increasing its conductance but not its open probability
source: Mg2+ thus appears to 'activate' G644P, by primarily increasing its conductance but not its open probability (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B and C).
evidence: Stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B and C.

claim: The current of G644P remains rectifying even at saturating Mg2+ concentrations
source: Interestingly, although Mg2+ exerts a qualitatively similar effect on G644P as Ca2+, the current remains rectifying even at saturating concentrations (Figure 2B).
evidence: Stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The activation by Mg2+ proceeds with a Hill coefficient close to unity
source: Moreover, in contrast to Ca2+, the activation by Mg2+ proceeds with a Hill coefficient close to unity and a maximum conduction rate at the intracellular entrance (σβ) that saturates at an intermediate value, suggesting that the binding site is likely occupied by a single Mg2+ ion (Figure 2B and C).
evidence: Stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2B and C.

claim: Three discrete levels of conductance correspond to the possible occupancies of the binding site with zero, one and two divalent cations bound
source: Taken together, our data show three discrete levels of conductance that correspond to the possible occupancies of the binding site with zero, one and two divalent cations bound (Figure 2C), consistent with a scenario where sequential Ca2+ binding lowers the energy barriers for anion conduction in a stepwise manner, as predicted by a simple Coulombic interaction.
evidence: Stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Gd3+ strongly increases the conductance at saturating concentrations even beyond the level induced by Ca2+
source: The model also describes the effect upon addition of the trivalent cation Gd3+, which strongly increases the conductance at saturating concentrations even beyond the level induced by Ca2+.
evidence: Stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: The increased conductance with Gd3+ is likely a consequence of the increased positive charge density in the binding site
source: This is likely a consequence of the increased positive charge density in the binding site and is manifested in the observed inward rectification of currents (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: Ca2+ and other di- and trivalent cations gate anion conduction in constitutively active mutants by an electrostatic mechanism
source: Our results suggest that Ca2+ and other di- and trivalent cations gate anion conduction in both constitutively active mutants by an electrostatic mechanism that involves neutralization of the negative charges in the vacant binding site.
evidence: Stated in the Results section and supported by experimental data.

claim: E654Q on a WT background exhibits the most severe phenotype among binding site mutants and does not show any activity even at high Ca2+ concentrations
source: Whereas on a WT background, E654Q exhibits the most severe phenotype among binding site mutants and does not show any activity even at high Ca2+ concentrations (Brunner et al., 2014; Lim et al., 2016; Tien et al., 2014), we observed basal and outwardly-rectifying currents in the mutant G644P/E654Q (PQ) whose steady-state current increases in response to Ca2+ addition (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Stated in the Results section with supporting citations and experimental data.

claim: The binding of a single calcium ion to the transmembrane site promotes anion permeation in the PQ mutant
source: The much lower conduction rate of the PQ mutant compared to G644P at saturating Ca2+ concentrations and a Hill coefficient close to one both suggest that in this mutant the binding of a single calcium ion to the transmembrane site promotes anion permeation, although less efficiently than the binding of two calcium ions in G644P, similar to the effect of Mg2+ (Figures 2 and 3A).
evidence: Stated in the Results section and supported by experimental data in Figures 2 and 3A.

claim: The rate of chloride conduction at the intracellular entrance at saturating Ca2+ concentrations is significantly higher in PR than in PQ
source: However, consistent with the hypothesis that a more positive potential at the binding site lowers the energy barrier for anion permeation, the rate of chloride conduction at the intracellular entrance at saturating Ca2+ concentrations is significantly higher than that observed for PQ (Figure 3B).
evidence: Stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The rate of chloride conduction at the intracellular pore entrance in the triple mutant PR2Q is increased compared to the double mutant PR both in the absence of Ca2+ and at saturating Ca2+ concentrations
source: As expected, the rate of chloride conduction at the intracellular pore entrance in the triple mutant PR2Q is increased compared to the double mutant PR both in the absence of Ca2+ and at saturating Ca2+ concentrations (Figure 3C).
evidence: Stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The contribution of individual charges in the binding site to conduction is additive
source: For electrostatic interactions, we expect the contribution of individual charges in the binding site to conduction to be additive.
evidence: Stated in the Results section and tested by experimental data.

claim: E705Q increases the rate of anion conduction to the same extent in both PQ5Q and PR5Q irrespectively of its background
source: At maximum Ca2+ occupancy, E705Q increases the rate of anion conduction to the same extent in both PQ5Q and PR5Q irrespectively of its background (Figure 3D,E), which emphasizes the orthogonal contributions of individual mutations (Figure 3F).
evidence: Stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3D, E, and F.

claim: Removal of a single calcium ion from the binding site partially decreases the positive potential observed in the fully bound structure
source: Consistent with the quantal effect of Ca2+ on anion conduction, removal of a single calcium ion from the binding site partially decreases the positive potential observed in the fully bound structure (Figure 4B).
evidence: Stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4B based on Poisson-Boltzmann calculations.

claim: Stepwise removal of charges in the binding site exerts progressively larger effects according to the number of charges neutralized
source: We also found that stepwise removal of charges in the binding site exerts progressively larger effects according to the number of charges neutralized (Figure 4C), as observed in our experiments.
evidence: Stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4C based on Poisson-Boltzmann calculations.

claim: An inverse and linear relationship exists between the energy barrier for chloride conduction at the intracellular pore entrance and the valence of the binding site
source: When the above mutants are analyzed collectively, we observed an inverse and linear relationship between the energy barrier for chloride conduction at the intracellular pore entrance and the valence of the binding site (Figure 4D).
evidence: Stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4D.

claim: The effective dielectric constant is around 160 in the vacant state and 90 for the single Ca2+-bound state
source: Assuming a Coulombic potential and using the distance measured from the Ca2+-bound structure, we estimated an effective dielectric constant of around 160 in the vacant and 90 for the single Ca2+-bound state.
evidence: Stated in the Results section based on analysis of experimental data.

claim: The estimated dielectric constant values indicate bulk solution-like aqueous properties consistent with the large water-filled intracellular vestibule
source: Although potentially inaccurate and physically unreasonable due to experimental limitations, these values indicate bulk solution-like aqueous properties that are consistent with the large water-filled intracellular vestibule observed in the Ca2+-bound structure (Figure 4D).
evidence: Stated in the Results section based on analysis of experimental data and structural information.

claim: Changes in the charge distribution at the neck affect Ca2+ binding
source: Reciprocally, changes in the charge distribution at the neck should affect Ca2+ binding.
evidence: Stated in the Results section as a hypothesis tested by experiments.

claim: Neutralizing mutations of Lys 588 and Lys 645 increase the potency of Ca2+
source: To test this hypothesis, we have investigated the effect of mutations of two residues, Lys 588 and Lys 645 (Figure 5A) located at the boundary between the intracellular vestibule and the neck, which lower the energy barrier for chloride conduction by contributing to the positive electrostatics of the pore (Paulino et al., 2017b). As expected, we found an increase in the potency of Ca2+ in neutralizing mutations of the respective residues to serine (Figure 5B,C), which is further enhanced upon the reversal of the charge by mutations to glutamate (Figure 5D,E).
evidence: Stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5B-E.

claim: A linear relationship exists between the change in binding energy and the valence at the intracellular pore entrance
source: Assuming that only the binding affinity of Ca2+ is affected, we observed a linear relationship between the change in binding energy and the valence at the intracellular pore entrance (Figure 5F), with a stronger sensitivity for Lys 645, which is in closer proximity to the Ca2+ binding site (Figure 5A) and thus might experience less solvent screening.
evidence: Stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5F.

claim: A direct effect of the ligand on the permeation properties of the open state is unique among ligand-gated ion channels
source: A direct effect of the ligand on the permeation properties of the open state is unique among ligand-gated ion channels and it is a consequence of the high positive charge density of Ca2+ and the location of its binding site in the immediate vicinity of the permeation path.
evidence: Stated in the Discussion section.

claim: The described effect is synergistic with a conformational change upon Ca2+ binding that opens a steric gate in the narrow part of the pore
source: The described effect is synergistic with a conformational change upon Ca2+ binding that opens a steric gate in the narrow part of the pore (Paulino et al., 2017a).
evidence: Stated in the Discussion section with supporting citation.

claim: In the absence of Ca2+, an electrostatic gate imposed by the vacant binding site would impede the access of chloride ions to the intracellular vestibule
source: In the absence of Ca2+, even in a sterically released conformation, which in this study was stabilized by mutations, an electrostatic gate imposed by the vacant binding site would impede the access of chloride ions to the intracellular vestibule (Figure 6).
evidence: Stated in the Discussion section and illustrated in Figure 6.

claim: The binding of Ca2+ releases the electrostatic gate by neutralizing the negative charges, enabling the open channel to conduct with full capacity
source: The binding of Ca2+ releases this second gate by neutralizing the negative charges, enabling the open channel to conduct with full capacity (Figure 6).
evidence: Stated in the Discussion section and illustrated in Figure 6.

claim: TMEM16A channels are dually gated by both steric and electrostatic mechanisms
source: Our findings thus provide novel mechanistic insight into the regulation of anion permeation in Ca2+-activated Cl- channels of the TMEM16 family and demonstrate that these channels are dually gated by both steric and electrostatic mechanisms.
evidence: Stated in the Discussion section as a conclusion from the experimental findings.

claim: The major conducting state in WT during activation is the open state with two Ca2+ ions bound
source: Since these plots reflect the weighted sum of the I-V relations of the open states with different Ca2+ occupancy, our results indicate that, during activation, the major conducting state in WT is the open state with two Ca2+ ions bound, whereas the contribution of open states with submaximal Ca2+ occupancy is minimal (Figure 1—figure supplement 2 and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: Stated in the Discussion section and supported by data in Figure 1—figure supplement 2 and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A,B.

claim: The findings provide direct evidence for the high cooperativity of TMEM16A activation
source: These observations thus provide direct evidence for the high cooperativity of TMEM16A activation.
evidence: Stated in the Discussion section as a conclusion from the experimental findings.

claim: The findings are relevant for the development of allosteric activators of TMEM16A for the treatment of obstructive airway diseases such as Cystic Fibrosis
source: Aside from their impact on membrane biophysics, our findings are particularly relevant for the development of allosteric activators of TMEM16A that may be beneficial for the treatment of obstructive airway diseases such as Cystic Fibrosis (Li et al., 2017; Mall and Galietta, 2015).
evidence: Stated in the Discussion section with supporting citations.

claim: Small molecules have the potential to increase the low open probability of the channel at low Ca2+ concentration
source: Although we anticipate that small molecules have the potential to increase the low open probability of the channel at low Ca2+ concentration, this might not suffice to promote robust Cl- efflux required to compensate for the loss of the chloride channel CFTR unless at the same time the electrostatic barrier at the intracellular pore entry is released, which would be the case for compounds with a positive net-charge or ones that at the same time increase the potency of Ca2+.
evidence: Stated in the Discussion section as a speculation about therapeutic implications.

claim: HEK293T cells were obtained directly from ATCC and tested negative for mycoplasma contamination
source: Obtained directly from ATCC; tested negative for myc oplasma contamination
evidence: Stated in the Key resources table.

claim: Mutants were generated with a modified QuikChange method using wild-type mouse TMEM16A(ac) as the template
source: Mutants were generated with a modified QuikChange method (Zheng et al., 2004) using the wild-type mouse TMEM16A(ac) as the template.
evidence: Stated in the Materials and methods section.

claim: Recordings were performed on inside-out patches excised from cells expressing the construct of interest
source: Recordings were performed on inside-out patches excised from cells expressing the construct of interest.
evidence: Stated in the Materials and methods section.

claim: Liquid junction potential was found to be consistently negligible given the ionic composition of the solutions and was therefore not corrected
source: Liquid junction potential was found to be consistently negligible given the ionic composition of the solutions and was therefore not corrected.
evidence: Stated in the Materials and methods section.

claim: All experiments were performed at 20 °C
source: All experiments were performed at 20 °C.
evidence: Stated in the Materials and methods section.

claim: The electrostatic potential along the pore was calculated by solving the linearized Poisson-Boltzmann equation in CHARMM
source: The electrostatic potential along the pore, identified using Hole (Smart et al., 1996), was calculated by solving the linearized Poisson-Boltzmann equation in CHARMM (Im et al., 1998; Brooks et al., 1983) on a 240 Å x 240 Å x 260 Å grid (1 Å grid spacing) followed by focusing on a 160 Å x 160 Å x 160 Å grid (0.5 Å grid spacing).
evidence: Stated in the Materials and methods section.
